title: Minimalist chrome — the header buttons lose their panel

steps.path: The strip along the top of the window
steps.headline: The header buttons, with no panel behind them
steps.changed: Every panel in the header is gone. The gear, Pages, Projects, the timer, the palette, the Chat/Terminal toggle, Session Files, Games, minimize/maximize/close — each is now its own glyph sitting straight on the wallpaper. The three group boxes that held them (the toggle's, the games button's, the caption buttons') no longer paint anything either.
steps.measured: header fills and borders now measure rgba(0,0,0,0); before, each button carried a 1px border and a 58% fill
steps.notice: The wallpaper runs unbroken across the whole header. The only thing marking a control is the mark itself and its shadow, so nothing reads as a box on the picture.
steps.risk: With no fill, the small icons have less to sit on over a busy wallpaper, so a textured pack can make them busier to pick out. The glyphs keep a soft shadow to stay separated from it.

steps.path: The message box and the strip under it
steps.headline: Left alone: the message box and chips keep their soft surface
steps.changed: Nothing here moved between the last round and this one. Each has the same fill, the same one-pixel edge and the same blur.
steps.measured: fill at 58% of the theme's own inset colour, blur(22px) — identical in both pictures
steps.notice: These keep the surface you approved, because a place to type needs to look like a place to type.
steps.risk: None. This is here so the two treatments sit side by side and you can see the difference between a surface and a control.
